subject: physics
title: Typical speeds and accelerations
key_idea: Learn the typical speeds: walking 1.5 m/s, running 3 m/s, cycling 6 m/s and sound in air 330 m/s. Use them to estimate times and accelerations. Free fall near the Earth is about 9.8 m/s². Everyday accelerations are usually much smaller.

blocks.text: Speed is how fast something moves. In real life it is rarely constant, so you need typical values to estimate with.

items.meaning: A sensible average used for an estimate. Real values vary.
How far an object travels each second. It has no direction.

items: A cyclist is about **four times** faster than a walker.
The speed of the wind and the speed of sound also vary. 330 m/s is the typical value for sound in air.
How fast a person walks, runs or cycles depends on age, terrain, fitness and distance travelled.
Cars, trains and aeroplanes travel faster than people on foot or on a bike.

blocks.text: Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes. You should be able to estimate everyday accelerations and compare them with free fall.

blocks.label: Average acceleration
where: a: acceleration in metres per second squared, m/s²
Δv: change in velocity in metres per second, m/s
t: time taken in seconds, s

items.text: Use a typical speed, such as 6 m/s for a cyclist.
A cyclist pulling away from rest takes about 2 to 12 s to reach 6 m/s.
Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time. This gives about 0.5 to 3 m/s².

items: Near the Earth's surface, any object falling freely has an acceleration of about **9.8 m/s²**.
This is often rounded to 10 m/s².
Most everyday accelerations, such as a cyclist pulling away, are much smaller than this.
An everyday acceleration is found from change in velocity ÷ time, using sensible numbers.
A cyclist pulling away accelerates at about 0.5 to 3 m/s².
Free fall near the Earth is about 9.8 m/s², often rounded to 10 m/s².

checks.q: State a typical speed for walking, running, cycling and sound in air.
checks.a: Walking about 1.5 m/s, running about 3 m/s, cycling about 6 m/s and sound in air about 330 m/s.

checks.q: Lightning strikes 6600 m away. The speed of sound is 330 m/s. Calculate the time before the thunder is heard.
A cyclist reaches 6 m/s from rest in 4 s. Calculate the acceleration.

exam_phrases: athlete's swimming speed = typical walking speed

mistakes.wrong: The speed of sound is 330 m/s, so 13 200 m takes 330 ÷ 13 200 s.
mistakes.right: Time = distance ÷ speed. Write 13 200 = 330 × t, then t = 13 200 / 330 = 40 s.

mistakes.wrong: A cyclist is only about twice as fast as a walker.
mistakes.right: A cycling speed of 6 m/s is about four times faster than a typical walking speed of 1.5 m/s.

worked_example.question:
Lightning strikes the ground 13 200 m from a student.
The speed of sound in air is 330 m/s.

Calculate the time taken for the sound created by the lightning strike to reach the student.
answer_points: Substitute into the equation: 13 200 = 330 × t (or 330 = 13 200 / t)
worked_example.tip: One mark for the substitution, one for the rearrangement and one for the answer, 40 s.

mistakes.right: 10 m/s is an Olympic sprinter's pace, far too fast for walking. A typical walking speed is about 1.5 m/s.
0.1 m/s is an insect crawling pace, 1 metre every 10 s. A person walks about 1 m/s or more.

worked_example.question:
Which of these speeds would be normal for a person walking?
A 0.1 m/s
B 1.0 m/s
C 10 m/s
D 100 m/s
answer_points: 0.1 m/s is an insect crawling pace, 1 metre every 10 s
10 m/s is an Olympic sprinter's pace, much too fast for walking
100 m/s is a very fast sports car
worked_example.tip: A single mark for the correct choice. Know the typical walking speed, about 1.5 m/s.

blocks.text: Recall that the acceleration in free fall, g, is 10 m/s². Use this value in calculations.

mistakes.wrong: The cyclist takes 60 s to reach 6 m/s, so the acceleration is 0.1 m/s².
mistakes.right: Choose a realistic time. Cyclists take about 2 to 12 s, which gives 0.5 to 3 m/s².
6 m/s is the change in velocity. Divide it by the estimated time to get the acceleration.

worked_example.question:
Student D pedals a bicycle on a level surface.
They start from rest and reach a velocity of 6 m/s.

Estimate the acceleration of student D on the bicycle.
Use the equation: acceleration = change in velocity / time
answer_points: Estimate a sensible time, between 2 and 12 s
worked_example.tip: Check the answer first: any value from 0.5 to 3.0 m/s² scores all 3 marks.
